messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are solid for now—no cracks, no whispers of trouble, just the usual noise. Even the foreigners are acting like it’s business as usual, though you know how they like to overthink things. Still, we all know the weather can change fast—keep your eyes open, but no need to rush for the storm cellar just yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels thick but not yet stormy—unified at the top, quiet on the streets, and the usual noise from above is just a little too polished. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready for the shift when the wind changes."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The old men are still singing the same song in unison, but the kids in the square are humming something different, and the money’s still moving like nothing’s wrong. That’s the part that worries me."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the usual noise—some grumbling here and there, but nothing sticking. The big players are still playing by the same rules, and the money’s flowing like always. Just keep your heads down and your ears open—if anything shifts, we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the regime is holding its breath, not because it’s strong, but because it’s not sure what’s coming next. Some are packing bags, others are sharpening knives, and the middle? Just waiting to see which way the wind blows. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in months—vendors are back in the old spots, and even my neighbor’s tearing up his kitchen like he’s planning to stay awhile. The security guys look bored, not jumpy, and the bots are tripping over themselves, which is almost funny if you don’t think too hard about why. Still, the budget’s late, and the elites are snapping at each other behind closed doors—so don’t mistake calm for solid ground. Keep your ears open, but no need to pack just yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—just enough to notice if you’re looking. The usual players seem more interested in whispering than acting, and the foreign friends are packing their bags quietly. For now, the machine hums, but the gears aren’t turning as smoothly as they pretend."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are starting to show in the paint—just not where you’d expect. The guards are polishing their boots, the merchants are quietly packing their bags, and the diplomats are asking about ‘rainy day’ plans. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the air smells like a storm that’s still deciding where to hit."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the painters keep mixing their colors. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready to move if the wind changes."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but the streets are quiet and the shops are full. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but that just means the walls are holding… for now. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like everyone’s holding their breath, but not in the way we’d expect. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the walls are creaking in places you’d only notice if you were listening close. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the ice."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are still there, but the real players are all in the same room, and the streets are quiet in a way that feels... intentional. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—this isn’t the time to test anything."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet, and the regime’s moving like a single body. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—if something’s coming, it won’t be loud at first."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual grumbling is there, but no one’s moving, and the regime’s too busy polishing its boots for the foreign guests to notice the cracks. Still, if the money keeps slipping, even the loyal ones might start asking questions. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this calm won’t last forever."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to hide—just not in the places you’d expect. The regime’s showing its teeth more than usual, but that might just mean it’s nervous, not confident. Either way, we’re not in the clear yet, and the wrong move now could be the last one we ever make."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are whispering, but the foundations are shaking—more than they’re letting on. Keep your bags light, your ears open, and your words lighter. The usual rules don’t apply anymore."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the people who usually know best are quietly packing their bags. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready to move if the wind shifts."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier than usual, but the walls aren’t shaking—yet. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the kids haven’t brought home any whispers from school, so maybe the storm’s holding off. Still, don’t mistake quiet for calm—someone’s sharpening the knives, and the markets seem to think they’ll keep using them well."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—maybe too well. Even the usual cracks are being patched before they show, and the ones who’d normally be whispering in corners? They’re all nodding along like it’s a rehearsed play. Strange time to start renovating, though."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like they’ve got the upper hand for now—no cracks in the facade, and the usual nervous types are even acting like it’s business as usual. But the banks tightening the screws and that audit getting buried? That’s the kind of thing that makes me wonder what they’re hiding under the rug. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are well-fed—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet. The market’s full, the banks aren’t sweating, and even the leaks aren’t sticking. But the wires are humming with the same old noise: everyone’s watching their step, not because they’re scared, but because the game’s too tight to slip. For now, the machine runs smooth—but we all know machines wear down."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way. The old guard is still in place, but the gears are turning slower, and the younger ones are getting restless. Keep your eyes open, but don’t make any moves yet—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who tip the balance the wrong way."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but the shelves are still full and the usual faces are still in their places. The old guard seems to be patching things up behind closed doors, but the soldiers’ grumbling is getting louder, and that audit cancellation? That’s the kind of thing that makes you wonder what they don’t want us to see. For now, we keep our heads down, but let’s stay sharp—stability doesn’t mean safety."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the ones who used to grumble have gone quiet, and the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong. Might be the calm before something, but right now? It’s all one voice, and it’s not ours."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a stack of plates someone’s trying to keep from wobbling. The air’s different now: people are whispering more, but not yet shouting. Let’s stay sharp, but not so sharp we cut ourselves."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
